What a /16 means

A /16 is a large site or campus block, the size of a historic Class B. 192.168.0.0/16 is a common private example.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /16 uses 16 network bits and leaves 16 host bits, so the block contains 65,536 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−16) − 2 = 65,536 − 2 = 65,534.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 172.16.0.1 255.255.0.0
!
access-list 10 permit 172.16.0.0 0.0.255.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 172.16.0.1/16

Linux

ip addr add 172.16.0.1/16 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /16?

65,534. A /16 has 65,536 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 65,534 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /16?

255.255.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.255.255.
